:::{#thm-gradient-of-linear}
#### Gradient of an entrywise inner product with a fixed matrix

Let $\matr{A}$ be a fixed $m \times n$ matrix, and for $\matr{W} \in \reals^{m \times n}$ define

$$g(\matr{W}) = \sumto{i}{m} \sumto{j}{n} W_{ij} A_{ij}$$

Then for every $\matr{W}$, $\nabla_{\matr{W}}\, g(\matr{W}) = \matr{A}$.
In particular, the gradient is constant: it does not depend on $\matr{W}$.

:::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-gradient-of-linear,
where $m = 2$, $n = 3$, and the entries of $\matr{A}$ are given.
The same argument works for every $\matr{A}$:
each $W_{ij}$ appears in exactly one term, multiplied by $A_{ij}$,
so $\derivf{g}{W_{ij}} = A_{ij}$.

:::
